items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh
items.claim: The text says the LORD told Moses to go to Pharaoh.
items.action: commanded Moses to go in unto Pharaoh

items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants
items.claim: The LORD is quoted as saying He hardened the hearts of Pharaoh and his servants.

items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: that I might shew these my signs before him
items.claim: The hardening is described as having a purpose: so the LORD could show His signs before Pharaoh.
items.mechanism: hardening lets the signs be shown

items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them
items.claim: The LORD is quoted as referring to things He did in Egypt and signs He did among the Egyptians.

items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son
items.claim: Another stated purpose is that the events would be told to later generations (sons and grandsons).
items.mechanism: passing the story down to later generations

items.tier: primary-text (scriptural narrative; claim attributed to speaker, not independently verified)
items.quote: that ye may know how that I am the LORD
items.claim: The final stated purpose is that the listeners would know that He is the LORD.
items.mechanism: signs and retelling lead to knowing the LORD
